title: G-L-H
hook: galut, exile, and gilui, revealing, share a root

segments.voice: Yesterday, A-L-M: olam, the world, and ne'elam, hidden. Your line was the world hides. Jeremiah's letter to the exiles first reached you on day eight hundred four; today, a root where hiding turns into showing.

A letter arrives in Babylon from the prophet Jeremiah, addressed to people carried off from Jerusalem. Other prophets have been promising it'll be over soon. Jeremiah tells them to build houses and live in them, plant gardens and eat what grows, marry, raise children. And then this: "seek the peace of the city whither I have caused you to be carried away captives, and pray unto the LORD for it: for in the peace thereof shall ye have peace." Pray for the city of your exile. The Hebrew under carried away captives is today's root.
screen: `A LETTER TO BABYLON.` → `BUILD, PLANT, MARRY.` → `SEEK THE PEACE OF THE CITY.`

segments.voice: G-L-H. Gimel, lamed, heh. Galut: exile. Gilui: revealing, uncovering. First, uncovering. The root's plainest sense is to lay something bare. In the book of Ruth, when Boaz wants to tell his relative about Naomi's field, the Hebrew says he wanted to uncover his ear: to let him know. Second, exile. The same letters mean to go into exile, to be carried off. Some readers hear the two meanings as one picture: exile is being uncovered, the covering of home pulled away. Third, God revealed. When Jacob builds an altar at Bethel, the text gives the reason: "because there God appeared unto him, when he fled from the face of his brother." Appeared is from this root, and notice when: while Jacob was running, in his own exile. Deuteronomy draws a line through the root too: "The secret things belong unto the LORD our God: but those things which are revealed belong unto us and to our children for ever." The revealed is what's handed to people to live by. Fourth, the rabbis. The Talmud teaches that wherever Israel was exiled, the Shechinah, God's presence, went with them. In this root, being sent away and being shown something share their letters. Jeremiah's letter is itself a revelation, mailed into an exile.
screen: `TO UNCOVER AN EAR.` · `EXILE: THE COVERING PULLED AWAY.` · `GOD APPEARED TO JACOB AS HE FLED.` · `THE PRESENCE WENT INTO EXILE TOO.` · then, large: `EXILE REVEALS.`

segments.voice: Bring back a time you were out of place: a new city, a new school, a hospital stay, a family you married into, a room where nobody spoke your language, and let the strangeness return for a moment. Then ask what it showed you that you couldn't have seen at home, about yourself, about kindness, about what you need, and hold that one thing. If you pray, you can remember Jeremiah's letter and pray for the place you're in now.
screen: `ONE TIME YOU WERE OUT OF PLACE.` · `WHAT DID IT SHOW YOU?` · `HOLD THAT ONE THING.`

segments.voice: G-L-H. Gimel, lamed, heh: galut, exile, and gilui, revealing. To be uncovered, and to be shown. Today's word.
Your line: exile reveals. The Talmud says the presence went into exile too. See you tomorrow.

chat.says: Why would Jeremiah tell exiles to pray for Babylon, the city that took them?
options: Build, plant, seek its peace, he said: in the city's peace, they'd have peace.
He wanted them to forget Jerusalem and become Babylonians for good.
He meant it as a test, to see who would refuse and stay loyal.
